content.text:
The pattern is best explained by Mg2CoWO6 (mp-1274182) alone.

- **Single-phase fits:** Mg2CoWO6 fits much better than the other candidates I tried. Its R-factor is 0.637, against 0.96 for Ba3Cr2O8 (mp-18913) and 0.98 for InFeO3 (mp-21094). Its peaks line up with all the main observed reflections. I didn't fit the other six candidates on their own.
- **Two-phase fits:** I fitted Mg2CoWO6 together with each of the other six candidates in turn. None helped much. The best pair, with CaY2O4 (mp-753815), only lowered R from 0.637 to 0.621. The second-phase weights stayed between about 7% and 12%. That is too small and too unfocused to show a real second phase.
- **Caveat:** R = 0.637 is still high, partly because the pattern is very noisy. One residual peak of about 19 near 30° remains. No candidate accounts for it, and the largest residual stays at 18.73 in every two-phase fit. That peak is the main reason my confidence isn't higher.

{"present": ["mp-1274182"], "confidence": 0.72, "note": "Mg2CoWO6 accounts for the main reflections and is by far the best single-phase fit; adding any other candidate as a second phase barely lowers the R-factor, and a residual peak near 30 degrees that no candidate explains remains."}
